questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: When searching for a study destination I wanted it to be in Asia, preferably South Korea, Japan or Singapore, as I wanted to know more about the Asian culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to find information upon arrival as most of the information had been sent by mail.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I found out by myself. There was an orientation for exchange students, but the spots were limited and overlapped the course registration period, thus I didn't attend it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: When it comes to South Korea it was fairly simple as goshiwons, which is sort of like a cheap room you rent sort of like kollegie in Denmark though not exclusively for students, are widely available.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you're opting for a goshiwon, find a place for exchange students, as you can make a lot of new friends there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There were set times where you could register for courses. Since the course registration opens for everyone at the same time,, you have to be fast to get your courses. Roughly a week before the semester started there was an after registration period, where you could drop courses. For full courses you could hope that an open spot would open up. Therefore at least in my case I had to refresh the course registration website about every 15 minutes to get my courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We received a mail with a detailed explanation of how it worked. You could also write a mail to the professors, departments and the Office of International Affairs for help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most of the classes I wanted to get. The only class I didn't get was restricted, so I couldn't get it anyways.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be sure to be on time for the course registration, as it will be hard to get all your courses if you don't apply for them immediately.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most of the courses were fairly easy with exception of my math course "Topics in Mathematics 2." This was an undergraduate course, but the contents were close to if not at PhD level, hence most of the other students who took the course were PhD students. Luckily the requirement to pass the course were low, but the contents of the course were far harder than one would expect from reading the course description and attending the first week of lectures (while we could still drop it and register for other courses.)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of learning by heart. Most of the exams were about how much you could remember and less about problem solving problems.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: "Basic Computing: First Adventures in Computing," "Korean History," "Survey in Vietnamese History," "Topics in Mathematics 2" and "Understanding Asian Philosophy."

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend "Understanding Asian Philosophy" and "Korean History" as they are courses that don't require too much work, while also learning a lot about the culture and history of Korea.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There is a mandatory health insurance in South Korea which is roughly 300 dkk a month

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Basically everything is cheaper than in Denmark. Especially eating out is pretty cheap here.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The SNU Buddy group was very fun for exchange students as they held a lot of events for exchange students. They also had a few clubs, but as an exchange student I didn't really have time for them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely the SNU Buddies.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Just explore Seoul as it is a big city by itself. In the Holidays you should try to go to Busan or Jeju.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: To me it was fairly easy. Most people just mind their own business on the street.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The locals are nice when you actually talk to them. Even when they don't speak English they try their best to communicate with you.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't take courses that require too much work as you want to experience life in Seoul instead of studying all day. Use the shuttle bus if you live close by SNU Station, as it is free. And if you travel a lot get a climate card.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you can you should get a Korean bank account. Also if you go to SNU then you will be offered to get your ARC through HireVisa, which you should totally do as it makes the process much easier and stress free.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The many new friends I made and also the experience of living in a completely different setting than what you are used to.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My one math course.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
